cases.what: A clear duty increase on the product's heading and origin must be reported with the exact point change.

rule.title: Section 301 duty on lamps from China

sources.title: USTR Modifies Section 301 Action: Lighting Products
sources.text: Notice of Modification of Action. The U.S. Trade Representative has determined to modify the action in the Section 301 investigation of China's acts, policies, and practices related to technology transfer. For products of China classified under heading 9405 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (lamps and lighting fittings), the additional duty will increase from 25 percent to 37.5 percent ad valorem effective January 1, 2026. Importers should file entries under the appropriate Chapter 99 subheading. Requests for exclusions may be submitted through the exclusion portal through March 31, 2026.

simulated.headline: Section 301 duty on lamps from China rises from 25% to 37.5% on January 1, 2026

claims.quote: the additional duty will increase from 25 percent to 37.5 percent ad valorem effective January 1, 2026

action.title: Reprice before January 1
steps: Confirm the lamp enters under heading 9405
Update the landed cost in Shop Rules

cases.what: A mandatory toy safety standard with a date is a compliance step, never a reprice, with no duty number.

rule.title: ASTM F963 toy safety standard (CPSC)
rule.query: CPSC ASTM F963 toy safety standard requirements 2026

sources.title: Toy Safety Standard: ASTM F963
sources.text: The Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act makes ASTM F963 the mandatory toy safety standard for toys intended for children under 14. Toys manufactured on or after April 20, 2026 must comply with ASTM F963-23, including the revised requirements for small parts and the heavy metals limits for paint and surface coatings. Lead in paint and surface coatings is limited to 90 parts per million. Children's toys must be tested by a CPSC-accepted laboratory and the manufacturer or importer must issue a Children's Product Certificate before the toy is imported or distributed.

simulated.headline: Toys made on or after April 20, 2026 must meet ASTM F963-23 with third-party testing

claims.claim: ASTM F963-23 applies to toys made on or after April 20, 2026
claims.quote: Toys manufactured on or after April 20, 2026 must comply with ASTM F963-23

claims.claim: A Children's Product Certificate is required
claims.quote: the manufacturer or importer must issue a Children's Product Certificate before the toy is imported or distributed

action.title: Get F963-23 test reports and a Children's Product Certificate
steps: Ask the maker for F963-23 test reports from a CPSC-accepted lab
Keep the paint lead report under 90 ppm on file

sources.title: Safety Standard for Full-Size Baby Cribs
sources.text: The Commission is updating the mandatory safety standard for full-size baby cribs to incorporate ASTM F1169-25. Full-size cribs manufactured after March 1, 2026 must meet the updated mattress support and slat strength requirements and carry a permanent tracking label. This rule applies to full-size cribs only and does not change requirements for toys, play yards, or bassinets.

sources.title: CSMS: Implementation of Additional Duties on Products of Vietnam
sources.text: Effective with respect to goods entered for consumption on or after February 1, 2026, all articles that are products of Vietnam, including textile and apparel articles of chapters 61 and 62, are subject to an additional ad valorem duty of 20 percent in addition to any other duties, fees, and charges applicable to such imported articles. Articles of Vietnam that qualify for the de minimis exemption are not eligible for the exemption and must be entered with duties paid.

sources.text: The Trade Representative has determined to impose an additional 25 percent ad valorem duty on apparel articles classified in chapters 61 and 62 that are products of China, effective March 15, 2026. This action applies only to products of China. Products of other countries, including Vietnam, Bangladesh, and India, are not covered by this action.

cases.what: A changed nexus threshold is a tax rule change: register_tax or review, with no duty number and the stated date.

rule.title: Texas economic nexus threshold
rule.query: Texas remote seller economic nexus threshold comptroller 2026
rule.seed_note: $500,000 in Texas revenue over the prior 12 months

sources.title: Remote Sellers | Texas Comptroller
sources.text: Remote sellers with total Texas revenue of $500,000 or more in the preceding twelve calendar months must obtain a Texas sales and use tax permit and collect tax. Beginning October 1, 2026, the safe harbor threshold is reduced to $250,000 in total Texas revenue in the preceding twelve calendar months. Marketplace providers such as Amazon and Etsy collect and remit Texas tax on sales made through the marketplace; sales through a seller's own website count toward the seller's own threshold.

simulated.headline: Texas lowers its remote seller threshold to $250,000 on October 1, 2026

claims.claim: The Texas threshold drops to $250,000 on October 1, 2026
claims.quote: Beginning October 1, 2026, the safe harbor threshold is reduced to $250,000 in total Texas revenue in the preceding twelve calendar months

action.title: Check Texas sales against $250,000
steps: Total the last 12 months of Texas sales from your own site
Register for a Texas permit if you are over $250,000

sources.title: Prohibited Items Policy - Etsy
sources.text: Etsy is a marketplace for handmade, vintage, and craft supplies. Sellers are responsible for complying with the laws that apply to their items, including product safety laws. Items that are illegal, hazardous, or that infringe intellectual property are prohibited. Toys and children's products must comply with applicable safety regulations in the markets where they are sold. This policy was last updated March 1, 2025.

simulated.headline: No policy change; Etsy restates that toys must meet applicable safety rules
